program.architecturalLanguage: crystal lattices, coordination polyhedra, pressure vessels, ceramic fortresses, exposed elemental strata, controlled oxidation, vitrification, metallic grain, and salt-like translucency

buildings.name: The Crystal Genome Foundry
buildings.purpose: Autonomous discovery of high-entropy oxides, carbides, nitrides, borides, intermetallics, metastable crystals, and compositionally complex ceramics
buildings.exteriorMotif: seven interlocking crystal-system wings, ordered-to-disordered diagrid, synthesis stack, and capsule tubes

buildings.name: The Monatomic Catalyst Spire
buildings.purpose: Single-atom and dual-atom catalysts, electrocatalytic water splitting, carbon-dioxide conversion, oxygen activation, and hydrogen production
buildings.exteriorMotif: three coordination arms suspending a mirror active-centre sphere above radial research wings

buildings.name: The Halide Ion Citadel
buildings.purpose: Solid-state alkali-metal batteries, halide and mixed-anion electrolytes, ion transport, interface stability, and mechanical failure suppression
buildings.exteriorMotif: four-layer salt-glass fortress with deep thresholds, dry trench, rain canopy, and six desiccant crystals

buildings.name: The Breathing Framework Ark
buildings.purpose: Metal-organic frameworks, porous coordination networks, selective gas separation, direct air capture, atmospheric water harvesting, and molecular sieving
buildings.exteriorMotif: porous node-and-strut arch, breathing triangular shutters, six gill towers, atmospheric ducts, and basins

buildings.name: The Solar-Fuels Leafworks
buildings.purpose: Artificial photosynthesis, photoelectrochemical water splitting, solar hydrogen, carbon-dioxide reduction, and light-driven inorganic catalysis
buildings.exteriorMotif: five pivoting mineral leaves, photoelectrode fields, water rills, gas-separation towers, and Solar Reaction Gate

buildings.name: The Nitrogen Triple-Bond Forge
buildings.purpose: Low-energy nitrogen fixation, mechanochemical ammonia synthesis, molecular molybdenum and iron catalysis, plasma activation, and cavitation chemistry
buildings.exteriorMotif: three acoustically isolated horizontal reactor drums held by a triple-bond steel exoskeleton

buildings.name: The F-Block Containment Monastery
buildings.purpose: Actinide chemistry, unusual f-element bonding, nuclear-fuel materials, isotope coordination, separations, and durable waste immobilization
buildings.exteriorMotif: five nested mineral walls around a single amber Shielded Lantern and enclosed transport rail

buildings.name: The Lanthanide Cascade Refinery
buildings.purpose: Rare-earth separation, electronic-waste recovery, redox-selective extraction, ionic-liquid processing, magnet recycling, and critical-metal circularity
buildings.exteriorMotif: seventeen progressively refined process towers, cascade columns, magnetic gantries, and sealed conveyors

buildings.name: The Polyoxometalate Basilica
buildings.purpose: Molecular metal-oxide clusters, multi-electron redox chemistry, water oxidation, molecular energy storage, photocatalysis, and switchable assemblies
buildings.exteriorMotif: faceted cobalt polyhedral dome, twelve cluster chapels, molecular rose window, busbars, and redox crown

buildings.name: The Quantum Oxide Terraces
buildings.purpose: Superconducting oxides, multiferroics, quantum paraelectrics, antiferromagnetic spintronics, topological phases, and strain engineering
buildings.exteriorMotif: six rotated epitaxial slabs separated by iridescent interfaces above isolated pylons and black-glass moat

buildings.name: The Megabar Diamond-Anvil Tower
buildings.purpose: High-pressure inorganic synthesis, superhydrides, extreme-state superconductors, planetary materials, and metastable phases
buildings.exteriorMotif: opposed diamond anvils compressed by monumental arches, tension cables, pressure rings, and brilliant compression band

buildings.name: The Molten-Salt Thermal Keep
buildings.purpose: Molten-salt chemistry, high-temperature electrochemistry, thermal storage, electrorefining, corrosion-resistant materials, and advanced reactor salts
buildings.exteriorMotif: ribbed ceramic fortress with six thermal stacks, glowing shielded conduits, radiator fields, and four ionic silos

buildings.name: The Biomineral Hybrid Conservatory
buildings.purpose: Bioinorganic chemistry, metalloenzymes, inorganic-microbial hybrids, nitrogenase-inspired catalysis, biomineralization, and metal-sulfur clusters
buildings.exteriorMotif: white porous mineral-reef shell with metallic veins, deposition panels, hydrothermal gardens, and transition bridge

buildings.name: The Carbon Mineralization Ramparts
buildings.purpose: Carbon-dioxide mineralization, carbonate curing, geopolymers, low-emission cement, mine-tailings utilization, and permanent carbon storage
buildings.exteriorMotif: coded experimental mineral strata, direct-air intake towers, erosion channels, and robotic construction rail

buildings.name: The Valence Nexus and Coordination Crown
buildings.purpose: Coordination chemistry, unusual oxidation states, metal-metal bonds, molecular magnets, low-valent main-group compounds, clusters, and Zintl phases
buildings.placementZone: Valence Avenue and Crystal Axis intersection
buildings.exteriorMotif: elevated periodic-block ring with eight ligand pylons around a suspended central-ion sphere and Coordination Crown
